the effect of coolant flow rate and blowing ratio on film cooling effectiveness distributions for a realistic turbine platform configuration.
the development of a new method for measuring the film cooling effectiveness distributions of a cooled turbine blade within a realistic cascade.
the effects of stator rotor purge and discrete film hole flows on film effectiveness distributions on a turbine blade platform.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of discrete film holes is essential for the protection of a turbine blade platform in a realistic stator-rotor cascade configuration.
the discrete film cooling holes are more effective in cooling the platform, but the upstream purge flow is still needed to protect the platform from the upstream passage induced flow.

film cooling effectiveness on a turbine blade platform is significantly affected by both the coolant flow rate through an upstream stator rotor seal and the coolant flow rate and blowing ratio through discrete film holes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the coolant flow rate and the discrete hole location are the two most important parameters to control in designing a cooled turbine platform.

film cooling effectiveness can be maintained on a turbine blade platform with a seal flow of 1.0% of freestream flow, while maintaining the effectiveness on the downstream half with a discrete hole film cooling flow of 1/3 that of the seal flow.

a stator rotor purge flow alone cannot adequately protect the downstream half of a turbine blade platform, but that a purge flow combined with discrete film cooling holes can provide a very effective cooling scheme.
The main takeaway from our work is that
discrete film cooling holes can be used to effectively cool the downstream portion of the passage while reducing the coolant flow rate through an upstream seal.
the coolant flow rate through discrete film holes can be reduced by as much as 50% while still providing the same level of protection as when the discrete holes are not used.
the coolant flow rate through a stator-rotor purge seal is an important parameter that must be controlled to maintain the effectiveness of a turbine blade platform.
